author: reek
body: The smallest program that puts highlighted Codex source on a real framebuffer through the real drawing path.

author: reek
body: The file manager's source preview is otherwise reachable only behind a first-boot wizard that wants a typed passphrase and an Ed25519 keypair, which is a great deal of machine to drive in order to look at one screen. This calls `gfl-source-lines` directly, with a buffer of ASCII source bytes exactly as a sector read would hand it over, so every line between the bytes and the pixels is the shipping one: the classifier, the run walk, `syn-colour`, and `gop-draw-text`.

author: reek
body: The bytes are built the way the medium holds them -- one ASCII byte per character, through `to-unicode` -- because that is what the image writer puts there and what the preview must read back. Filling the buffer with CCE code points instead would make the probe agree with a reader that was wrong.

author: reek
body: Five lines, chosen so the frame cannot pass by accident: a header, a prose line whose first word is `cites`, the same word as a real directive one space further in, a keyword-and-number line, and a string. If the classifier were bypassed and the whole buffer drawn in one colour, the prose and directive lines would be indistinguishable, which is precisely what the previous hex view could not tell you either.

author: reek
body: The probe has to still be running when the frame is taken, because codex-vm captures the framebuffer at the delay and a guest that has already exited leaves nothing to capture. A short spin ran out in under a second and produced no screenshot at all, which reads exactly like a drawing path that wrote nothing.
